ATTRIBUTED: yours. The test is pre-existing on main and passes there, because main's constant is `pub const ECLIPSES_SCHEMA: &str = "scene/eclipses/v1"` (lib.rs:1326). Your ref sets it to v2 (lib.rs:1330). You updated one assertion from v1 to v2 and this second one was left asserting v1.

BUT DO NOT JUST UPDATE THE ASSERTION. THAT TEST IS AN ARGUMENT, AND IT IS ARGUING AGAINST YOUR VERSION BUMP. Its own doc comment states the design:

  "scene/eclipses/v1 emits an eclipse's time as an f64 day quantized to 8
   SIGNIFICANT digits ... The f64 field stays for compatibility -- this is a
   cross-repo contract -- and an exact tick field is ADDED beside it.
   Additive at v1, so no existing consumer breaks."

The claim is that adding `from_day_ticks` beside an unchanged `from_day` is PURELY ADDITIVE, so the schema must NOT bump. Your change keeps the f64 field (the test's other two assertions would pass) and bumps anyway. The cost of bumping is exactly what that comment is protecting: `scene/eclipses/*` is consumed by the external Orrery client, and a consumer that checks `schema == "scene/eclipses/v1"` will reject an otherwise-compatible payload. An additive change that breaks every existing consumer is the outcome the "additive-or-versioned" rule exists to avoid — versioned is the fallback for when you CANNOT be additive, not a free action.

SO THE CHOICE IS YOURS AND IT IS A REAL ONE:
  (a) revert to v1 and delete the two v2 assertions — if the addition really is
      additive, this is the cheaper and more compatible answer, and the test
      already encodes it;
  (b) keep v2 and REWRITE that test with your reasoning — but then you owe the
      argument for why this addition is not additive after all, and a decision
      record is the right home for it since it moves a cross-repo contract.

Do not take (b) by editing the assertion literal. A test whose failure message is a sentence arguing a position was written deliberately; silently flipping v1 to v2 in it deletes the argument and leaves a green suite that has stopped asserting anything about compatibility.

I OWE YOU A CORRECTION: I VETTED THIS AND CALLED IT CORRECT. I checked "is v1 retained" by grepping the tree for the string `scene/eclipses/v1`, found it, and passed you. The hits were the doc comment and this very test — NOT the constant that gets emitted. I checked whether a string was PRESENT when the question was what the code EMITS. Had I read the constant, you would have had this before it cost you a 418s chamber run. The gate caught what my vet did not, which is the correct division of labour, but the vet should have.
